where: 1.17, display 'f(k + v ε) = k + (u(v) + D d k)'
scan: f(k + v ε) = k + (u(v) + D d k) : nothing follows the closing parenthesis
note: The ε of the image is missing: elements of D_W(K) are written k + wε (p. 45), and the composition law (uu', D + uD') two lines below follows from f(k + vε) = k + (u(v) + D dk)ε. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Lemma 1.18 (2), display '[A((k, D))] : [A(D_K'(K))] → [A(D_K'(K))] is x ⟼ x + γ(D)'
scan: [A((k, D))] : a clear typewriter k (the 1 of F(1, D) further down has its flag)
note: The map acting as x ⟼ x + γ(D) is the one induced by (1, D): cf. 'F(D) = F(1, D)' and the general formula x ⟼ u(x) + γ(D) in (3); k is the key next to l, the typewriter's 1. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Proof of 1.18, display of the maps i and p, 'i ; V ↪ V ⊕ K'^n'
scan: i ; V : a semicolon after i (p is followed by a colon)
note: Shift slip on the ;/: key. The TeX keeps the printed semicolon. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Proof of 1.18, same display, 'p : V ⊕ K'^n ⟶ K^n ,'
scan: target K^n without a prime (the source V ⊕ K'^n has it)
note: p is the projection of V ⊕ K'^n onto the summand K'^n (the right-hand column of the diagram on p. 48 is K'^n ⊗ A). The same prime is missing in 'x : K^n → V' on p. 48. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: First line, 'the following diagramm is commutative'
note: Spelling slip. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Diagram after 'the following diagramm is commutative', left vertical arrow V ⊗ A → V ⊗ A
scan: label F(D) typed to the right of the downward arrow
note: The swap mark ' sets the label to the left of a downward arrow; without it tikz-cd sets it to the right, as printed (the file's own comment block also records the label to the RIGHT of the shaft).

where: Same diagram, middle vertical arrow (V ⊕ K'^n) ⊗ A → (V ⊕ K'^n) ⊗ A
scan: label F(i,D) typed to the right of the downward arrow
note: As for F(D): the swap mark puts the label on the left; the print has it on the right.

where: Same diagram, label of the middle vertical arrow 'F(i,D)'
scan: F(i,D) with a comma; the formula four lines below has F(i D)
note: The middle vertical arrow is the endomorphism F(iD) = F(1, iD) of (V ⊕ K'^n) ⊗ A (an F(i,D) would be a map out of V ⊗ A); the text applies F(i D) to Σ e_i a_i below. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring and does not overlap the label-side edit.

where: 'Let x : K^n → V be a map'
scan: x : K^n → V, K without a prime
note: x is defined on the summand K'^n of V ⊕ K'^n (1_V + x is composed with i in the next sentence), as for the target of p on p. 47. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Display 'F(i D)(Σ e_i a_i) = Σ e_i a_i + a (a ∈ V ⊗ H) , then'
note: a lies in V ⊗ A = F(V): by the right-hand square of the diagram F(iD) does not change the K'^n ⊗ A component; no H is defined at this point (H is introduced after Theorem 1.20). The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Display after 'Hence,', third line 'u G(D) = F(u D) (for any u : V → W)'
note: Applying (u ⊗ 1) ∘ F(D) = F(uD) ∘ (u ⊗ 1_A) (p. 47) to F(D)(y) = y + G(D) gives u G(D) = G(uD); F(uD) is a map, not an element. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Definition 1.19 (2), 'A formal versal object ξ in Â , with image (R, s)'
scan: Â with its hat but no underline under the A (the Â of (1) and the two Hom_Â subscripts are underlined)
note: The category letter lost its underline. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Definition 1.19 (2), last line, 'i.e. φ_2-φ_2 = D s'
scan: φ_2-φ_2 = D s : both indices are 2
note: (1, D)(φ_1) = φ_2 means φ_2 = φ_1 + D s, i.e. φ_2 - φ_1 = D s. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

scan: [A(D_K'(K))] with no underline under the A
note: The cofibered groupoid A is underlined everywhere else, including twice in the statement of 1.20 itself. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.

where: Section 2, first paragraph, 'out of ξ alone..One has to know'
scan: alone..One : a full stop, then a second smaller dot (a speck between them), no space before One
note: Doubled full stop. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.
